The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 09.08.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 09.08.2024 at about 01.50 p.m., petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EB-7188 proceeding opposite to Mi Showroom, cautiously, observing the traffic rules.

At that time a Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, came at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and rider were fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Arogya Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance, food, transport and other charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 19 years, the petitioner was student and also working as Computer operator and earning Rs.16,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.
Further this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending Auto-rickshaw and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further this respondent submits that, the petitioner was minor and was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet and without a valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

It is further submitted that, the accident in question took place solely due to the carelessness and negligent of the petitioner and contributed to the cause of the accident and the degree of negligence on the part of the minor petitioner was on the higher side.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings framed the following issues are as under:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503 on 09.08.2024 at about 01.50 p.m., opposite to MI Showroom, Ramamurthy Nagar Main Road, Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and closed his side.
On the other hand, Assistant Manager of respondent No.1 Insurance Company is examined as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
8.
ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,

Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the MLC, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch, Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificates, Ex.P.8 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is the Notice U/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.10 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.11 and 12 are the Discharge summaries,
Ex.P.13 is the Medical Bills and Ex.P.14 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 09.08.2024 at about 01.50 p.m.,
petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EB-7188 proceeding opposite to Mi Showroom, cautiously, observing the traffic rules.

At that time a Auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, came at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and rider were fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Arogya Hospital,
wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.209/2024.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 281, 125(b) of BNS.
11.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the K. R. Puram Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 209/2024.
The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.2 along with complaint.
12. Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.3 (MLC Extract), Ex.P.4 (Spot Mahazar) and Ex.P.5 (Sketch) clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.8, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle U/s. 125(a) and 281 of BNS.
The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
13. On the other hand, assistant manager of respondent Insurance company is examined as RW.1 and got marked 03 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.

RW.1 deposed in his evidence that, petitioner was minor riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet and without valid and effective driving license and dashed against the auto- rickshaw, thereby he contended that, the accident is caused due to the rash and negligent act of minor petitioner/rider of the motorcycle.

During the course of cross-examination he admits that, charge-sheet is submitted against the driver of the insured vehicle and further he admits that, as per the police documents nowhere it is mentioned that, petitioner was rider of the motorcycle at the time of accident.

14. Learned counsel for Insurance Company argued that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent act of petitioner and at the time of accident the petitioner was the rider of the motorcycle,
but only in order to get the compensation they have filed false complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
In support of his argument he relied upon the Ex.R.3 and Ex.P.11.
On perusal of Ex.R.3 i.e., Medical Legal Register issued by Sri Arogya Hospital.

On perusal of said register it Nikhil vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128853595/
4 reveals that, as on the date of accident the petitioner was riding the bike.

sentences.text: Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 also it reveals that, petitioner was driving in a two-wheeler vehicle with his friend.
These two documents are issued by the Sri Arogya Hospital's authorities, when the petitioner was admitted for first aid treatment.
Further, it is not the case of the petitioner that, he has not taken any treatment from the said hospital.
Infact, petitioner himself has produced the Ex.P.11.
As such, this Court opine that, as on the date of accident petitioner was riding the two-wheeler.
15. In view of above discussion, this Court opine that, as on the date of accident petitioner was rider of the motorcycle at the time of accident.

It must be noted that, in the cross-examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the accident had happened because of the negligence on his part, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.1 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that,
respondent No.1 has admitted the accident
. In other words, it is well settled that, suggestion is the reflection of the case of the opponent.
16. As stated above, respondents have not produced any evidence before this court to show that, the accident is not caused due to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, the above discussion makes it clear that, except barred allegations, the respondent No.1 has not made any efforts to show that, the accident had happened because of the fault of the petitioner.
It is well settled that, in Motor vehicle accident compensation cases, the strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others Vs. HRTC.

sentences.text:
Thus, I opine that, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, the accident had happened because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503.
17.
Learned counsel for Insurance Company argued that, accident is caused due to the negligent act of minor petitioner.
As such, he argued that, insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
On the other hand, learned counsel for petitioner argued that, charge-sheet is submitted against driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s 125(a) and 281 of BNSS.

As such,
question of negligence on the part of petitioner does not arise.

At this stage it is profitable to refer the following decisions in order to assess the above argument,
(i) 2018 ACJ 982 between Shaktisih Zala Vs. Zala Ranvirsinh Ranubha and others, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat observed that, once driver of offending jeep is held to be solely negligent for the accident, motorcyclist may be minor and may not be having license cannot be held to be negligent or contributory negligent.
(ii) 2008 ACJ 1834 between Sudeer Kumar Rana Vs. Surender Singh and others, wherein Apex Court at para No.8 opine that, 'If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.

It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini-truck which was being driven rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any license but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two- wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how,

HRTC and others, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court observed that, to prove the contributory negligence there must be cogent evidence and in the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the plea of contributory negligence it cannot be held minor could not have been permitted to drive the scooter.

sentences.text: 18. Upon perusal of the facts and circumstances in the above stated Judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as High Courts, it can be seen that, once driver of offending vehicle is held to be solely negligent for the accident, motorcyclist may be minor or may not be having license cannot be held to be negligent or contributory negligent.
Even if petitioner rode the vehicle it does not make much difference in view of above discussion.
19. The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.7 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to Manipal Hospital on 10.08.2024.
Further, Wound Certificate shows that, the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.

Further, in the said Wound Certificate it is mentioned that,
petitioner admitted to the hospital with alleged history of RTA.
These facts are not denied by the respondent No.1.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Arogya Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

21. In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and produced Discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.11 and Ex.P.12.
Further the petitioner has produced the wound certificates marked at Ex.P.7, wherein the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
22. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 17 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.13 to the tune of Rs.72,182/-.

23. Further the petitioner contended that, prior to the accident he was working as Computer Operator and was drawing salary of Rs.16,000/- per month, but in support of his contention he has not produced any documents before this Court.

sentences.text: In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that he has become permanently disabled.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- including the medical expenses.
25. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AF-3503 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 125(a) and 281 of BNS.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 28.12.2023 to 27.12.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 09.08.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
26. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
27. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
